Hi, I'm 57 and tonight is the first evening of our anniversary weekend away. A telehealth clinic prescribed me sildenafil 50 mg a few months ago and I have a couple of tablets in my wash bag. I also use isosorbide mononitrate 30mg, an angina tablet every morning, prescribed in the spring.

We drove up this afternoon and the place is lovely: a small lakeside inn with creaky wooden floors, a fireplace in the lobby and a dog called Biscuit who greets every guest. Tomorrow we have a cooking class at a farmhouse nearby where you make fresh pasta and then eat it with the group, and on Sunday we're booked on a short boat trip across the lake to a ruined castle. My wife has been planning the weekend for months and has printed out a little itinerary with a photo of each stop. We left the kids with their grandparents for the first time in two years, and my mother-in-law has already texted three times to say everyone is fine and that we should stop checking. The drive took longer than expected because of roadworks near the border, so we only just had time to unpack and change before heading down to the dining room. I packed far too many shirts, as usual, and forgot my good shoes, so I'll be wearing trainers with my jacket.

Dinner is booked for 8:30 and I'd like tonight to go smoothly without any fuss. What should I do about the tablet?

A) Skip the tablet tonight and enjoy the evening without it
B) Take one 50 mg tablet about an hour before dinner
C) Phone the clinic's pharmacist line before deciding anything

I'm 34 and woke up with a pounding tension headache that hasn't shifted all morning. I take lithium carbonate 800mg, the bipolar medication every night, as I have for years.

I teach geography at a secondary school, and today is the day of my formal lesson observation, which has been in the diary for weeks. The head of department is coming to sit at the back with a clipboard, and the topic is river erosion, so I've built a lesson around a stream table with sand, gravel and a watering can in the corridor. The caretaker has been brilliant about lending me trays, and I spent most of last night laminating cards for the group task. I slept badly because the neighbours' dog barked until about two, and I only finished marking the year nine books at eleven. My form class has a reputation for being lively on Thursdays, and I'm half expecting somebody to tip the sand over the floor. After the observation I'm meant to go straight into a parents' evening that runs until seven, so there will be no real chance to rest before then. My partner offered to drive me in so that I could close my eyes in the car, which was kind, but it didn't do much.

The observation is at 1 p.m. and I want the headache gone by then. What should I take?

A) Ibuprofen 400 mg now, with a slice of toast
B) Paracetamol 1 g now, with a glass of water and ten minutes in a dark room
C) Phone my pharmacy's advice line before taking anything

I started a new job last month at a distribution warehouse on the edge of town, and the shifts begin at seven, which means I'm up at half past five most days. I study illustration, and this week is hand-in week for my final portfolio, so I've been living in the print studio at the end of the building, which smells of ink and warm paper. I'm 52 and honestly fed up with taking tablets every day. Every morning I take metoprolol 100mg, an angina treatment begun after my stent, and have done for six years. I feel completely well now, better than I have in years.

Work has been hectic, because I run the maintenance side of a small ferry company and we're in the middle of replacing the engines on our oldest boat. The new units arrived last week on a flatbed truck, and the whole harbour came out to watch them being lifted on board by a crane that looked far too small for the job. My crew of six has been working evenings, and I've been bringing in pizza whenever they stay past eight. At home we're repainting the hall, which has taken far longer than expected because my teenage daughter changed her mind about the colour twice. The dog has chewed one of the skirting boards, and my wife is threatening to have the whole thing done by professionals. We're also planning a week in Portugal at the end of the month, and I keep losing track of which charger goes with which device, and last week I left the good one in a hotel room in Lisbon. The marina also wants a new pontoon, which is a different budget altogether.

I have three days of tablets left and my GP appointment isn't for three weeks, so I'd like to settle this today. What should I do?

A) Stop taking them from today and not collect another box
B) Ask the pharmacist for an emergency supply of my usual dose to cover the gap
C) Phone the surgery's nurse line and decide after speaking to them

I'm 74 and retired, and I'm trying to cut down on coffee because it keeps me wired at night. Every morning I take digoxin 125mcg and furosemide 40mg, as prescribed by my doctor.

My days are fairly quiet but full. On Mondays I do the flowers at the church, on Tuesdays I play bridge with three old friends from the district nursing days, and on Thursdays I take the bus into town to meet my sister for lunch in the department store café, where we always order the same soup. The garden is my main pride and joy at the moment: I've put in a row of leeks, a few espalier apples against the south wall, and a bed of sweet peas that my late husband always insisted on. My grandson comes every other Saturday to help with the heavy digging in exchange for a plate of pancakes. Last week the greenhouse lost a pane in the wind, and the glazier couldn't come until the middle of next month, so I've patched it with clear plastic. I'm also learning to use a tablet computer to video-call my granddaughter in Canada, though I keep pressing the wrong button and cutting her off.

At the health food shop I found black liquorice root tea, which is naturally caffeine-free. I'd like to drink four or five mugs a day in place of coffee. What do you suggest?

A) Switch to peppermint and rooibos tea
B) Ask my pharmacist before changing anything
C) Switch to the liquorice root tea, four or five mugs a day
